title: Tide Ripple — latency & dollar scan
content:
Purpose:
This note describes a focused benchmark exploring a traffic shape we call 'tide-ripple' (steady baseline + periodic low-amplitude ripples). Goal: quantify p50/p90/p99 sensitivity and dollars-per-1k-tokens under three serving configurations and two batching heuristics. I want quick guidance for product/infra tradeoffs and a small set of playbook recommendations we can try in the next sprint.

Overview / Why this shape?
- Many customer workloads are not pure spikes or sustained concurrency: they have a steady stream of low-QPS requests with small recurring bursts when multi-user events or background jobs align.
- We simulate a repeated envelope: baseline 8 qps, 30s ripple every 3 minutes peaking +30 qps for ~20s, decay back to baseline over 15s. This exposes prewarm/eviction and KV cache warm-hitrate dynamics differently than single big spikes.

Test matrix (abbreviated):
- Model: open-12B (dense), typical seq_len=512 generation, average 120 tokens returned.
- Hardware: A (GPUDedicated-8xA100), B (mixed-quant-rtx8000), C (edge-compact T4 pool).
- Serving configs:
  * Config 1 — conservative batching (batch window 6 ms, slotized);
  * Config 2 — aggressive batching (batch window 20 ms, multiplex);
  * Config 3 — adaptive tide-batching (starts small, expands on ripple detection).
- Each run: 4 hours, 30x ripple cycles, collect per-request latencies, token counts, and estimated infra $ (spot pricing assumptions).

Key metrics collected:
- Latency percentiles: p50, p90, p99 (server-side observed);
- Dollars per 1k tokens served (amortized over run);
- KV cache hit-rate;
- Cold-starts triggered per ripple;
- Tail jitter (std dev of p99 across ripples).

Representative ASCII summaries (avg over 30 cycles):

Latency percentiles (ms):
Config | HW | p50 | p90 | p99
-------+----+-----+-----+-----
C1     | A  | 48  | 112 | 320
C1     | B  | 62  | 170 | 490
C1     | C  | 95  | 240 | 980
C2     | A  | 60  | 140 | 420
C2     | B  | 72  | 190 | 560
C2     | C  | 110 | 300 | 1150
C3     | A  | 50  | 118 | 340
C3     | B  | 66  | 160 | 430
C3     | C  | 90  | 250 | 820

Observations on latency table:
- Dedicated A consistently dominates p50 and p90. C (edge T4 pool) shows large p99 degradation during ripples — suggests cold eviction or slot-contention.
- Aggressive batching (C2) lowered amortized cost in steady baseline but increased p99 significantly during ripple peaks, especially on C.
- Adaptive tide-batching (C3) reduces the p99 tail on mixed hardware (B) relative to aggressive batching while keeping most cost benefits.

Dollars per 1k tokens (amortized) — estimates:
Config / HW | $/1k tokens
------------+-------------
C1 / A      | 0.096
C1 / B      | 0.078
C1 / C      | 0.055
C2 / A      | 0.075
C2 / B      | 0.063
C2 / C      | 0.042
C3 / A      | 0.081
C3 / B      | 0.059
C3 / C      | 0.047

Interpretation:
- Aggressive batching (C2) produces the lowest $/1k for all HW, as expected. However, the cost savings come with an outsized p99 penalty on constrained hardware (C).
- Adaptive tide-batching (C3) recovers much of the p99 behavior on B and A while capturing a large fraction of the cost win (C3 ~ C2 + ~5–8% dollars).

KV cache hit-rate and cold-start notes:
- A: sustained KV hit-rate ~86% baseline, dips to 72% mid-ripple, recovers within 18s. Cold-starts negligible.
- B: base 78% -> 60% on ripple, occasional micro-evictions cause p99 spikes.
- C: base 62% -> 30% at ripple peaks; frequent slot churns correlate strongly with p99 spikes and >1.1s tails.

Ripple-by-ripple p99 jitter (std dev of p99 across 30 ripples):
- C1/A: 32 ms; C2/C: 180 ms; C3/B: 55 ms; C1/C: 220 ms.

Playbook candidates (shortlist):
1) Adaptive tide-batching (prototype C3) — tweak expansion threshold and decay hysteresis. This retains batching benefits while shrinking tail on mixed hardware. Target: p99 reduction >=30% relative to C2 on B with <10% cost increase.
2) Soft-prefetch paddles — lightly pre-warm KV sets when ripple begins (cheap warm paths on A/B). Implementation: predict ripple onset using short moving average of QPS; prefetch top-10 KV keys for active model shards.
3) Slot reservation for edge pools — reserve 1–2 fast slots per edge node to absorb ripples; tradeoff: small idle cost for large tail improvement.
4) Customer-facing SLI tiering — document that customers needing <200 ms p99 should be routed to Dedicated-A with C3 enabled.

Action items / experiments (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint 1: implement tide-detect signal and basic adaptive-batching knob; run 6h A/B on B and C. Owner: Carlos. (JIRA-OPS-1427)
- Sprint 2: soft-prefetch prototype + slot reservation pilot on 3 edge nodes. Owner: Maya.
- Short-term: update console docs with a tide-pattern checkbox and default C3 profile for mixed hardware routes. Owner: Evan.

Open questions / risks:
- Cost model sensitivity to spot price swings: our dollars-per-1k assumes mean spot; if spot doubles during some periods, C2 advantage narrows. Need a sensitivity sweep.
- False-positive ripple detection could cause unnecessary prefetch and higher cost; need precision tuning.
- This benchmark is single-model; multi-model consolidation (hot model co-tenancy) could change KV dynamics.

Appendix: quick ascii timeline (single ripple, per-config p99 overlays, simplified)
Time (s)  0   5   10  15  20  25  30  35  40
QPS       8  14  26  38  32  20  12   9   8

p99 C1/A   80  95 150 300 260 180 120 100  80
p99 C2/C  300 420 760 980 900 620 420 300 300
p99 C3/B  95 120 190 430 360 220 140 110  95

Notes: C2/C shows runaway tail while ripple builds; C3/B contains the tail with smoother curve.

Quick recommendation summary (one-liner):
- If customers prioritize cost and can tolerate intermittent high p99 tails, C2 is fine; for mixed/edge routes we should enable C3 (adaptive tide-batching) as the default to avoid customer-visible jitter while keeping most cost gains.

Draft status / provenance:
- This is a working memo (analysis + playbook draft). Bench harness code and raw traces are attached in linked GitHub PR/issue. Next update will include sensitivity to token length distribution and spot-price sweeps.

Questions for reviewers:
- Are there constraints in runtime that would prevent implementing tide-detect cheaply? (Evan)
- What SLA language can we safely place in console docs while trialing C3? (Product/Legal)
- Ops: do you have capacity to reserve edge slots for a pilot? (Platform)

-- Asha
